$schema_note: WELDER hero video case. Every leaf is tagged in provenance.json by JSON path. Numbers are measured from the raw sensor CSV unless the provenance says otherwise.

labels.note: Illustrative traceability labels. The dataset has no operator, station, part, or WPS fields; the real identifier is raw_data.part_no.

raw_data.dataset: Intel Robotic Welding Multimodal Dataset (local mirror)

image.note: plate_front is the front view with the printed part-number label repainted by the project destick pipeline; bead crops are the project's label-removed gold crops (run200 idx 180 / views idx 168).

visual.location: WELD TOE (lower toe, middle-to-right of bead)
visual.morphology: CONTINUOUS TOE GROOVE; UNEVEN BEAD WIDTH
visual.source_statement: A dark, continuous linear groove/depression is visible along the lower weld toe, most pronounced through the middle-to-right portion of the bead. The weld metal does not consistently blend into and fill the toe region, which is direct visual evidence of Undercut.

wire_feed.state: RAMPING (typical of every weld in this cell)

reference.population: good fillet Fe410 welds, n=140, per-weld arc-on statistics

wps_window.note: p5-p95 of per-weld arc-on means over good fillet Fe410 welds; stands in for a qualified WPS window

symbolic_knowledge.kb: WELDER-KB (kb-v1, GraphRAG index over 45 welding documents; 4,986 entities, 9,855 relationships)

defect_entity.title: UNDERCUT
defect_entity.definition: an irregular groove at the toe of a run in the parent metal

cause_edges.text: High welding current will also cause undercut; this is generally associated with the need for a high travel speed to avoid overfilling of the joint
Travel speed that is too fast, without using enough filler metal, is a common cause of undercut
Excessive voltage is a common cause of undercut
Excessive arc length is noted as contributing to undercut
Incorrect gun angle, with arc focus too much on the bottom plate and not enough on the top plate, can create undercut
Poor welder technique can cause undercut
High arc pressure can push molten metal away from the toes, causing or promoting undercut

no_edge.text: kb-v1 contains ARC INSTABILITY (degree 15) but no edge from it to UNDERCUT

remedy_edges.source: ANGLE TORCH TO PUSH WELD METAL TO FILL MELTED GROOVE

symbolic_knowledge.retrieval_query: What process conditions and physical mechanisms cause undercut in CO2 MAG (GMAW) welding of steel, and how can it be prevented or corrected?

trigger.simple_hypothesis: Electrical process instability caused the defect
trigger.verdict: OBSERVATIONS INCONSISTENT WITH THE SIMPLE HYPOTHESIS → ESCALATE TO SLOW REASONING

candidate_hypotheses.name: Electrical instability
candidate_hypotheses.predicts: current and voltage fluctuate during the weld
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: current CV 0.039, voltage CV 0.028 on the plateau; no instability window inside the arc-on plateau; kb-v1 has no ARC INSTABILITY → UNDERCUT edge

candidate_hypotheses.name: Excessive heat input (current above window)
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: high arc energy melts a toe groove faster than filler can refill it
candidate_hypotheses.predicts: current above the WPS window with a stable arc
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: plateau mean 279 A vs window 119-182 A (rule check: violated); wire feed 124 vs 41 mm/min reference; kb-v1 edge WELDING CURRENT → UNDERCUT

candidate_hypotheses.name: Travel speed too fast
candidate_hypotheses.predicts: high travel speed for the given deposition
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: nominal robot speed 30 vs 25 cm/min for good welds; no travel-speed sensor in the log

candidate_hypotheses.name: Torch / work angle
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: arc focused on the bottom plate
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: lower-toe predominance in the image; no angle sensor

reasoning.explanation: MECHANISM-CONSISTENT EXPLANATION: heat input above the qualified window (current ~279 A against a 119-182 A window) with a stable arc; toe groove consistent with WELDING CURRENT → UNDERCUT. Contributions of travel speed and torch angle cannot be separated without travel-position or angle sensing.

teacher_ranked_causes.factor: Excessive or locally elevated arc energy during the active weld interval
Transient current peak and high-current operating band causing enhanced toe melting and molten-pool displacement
Unstable feed progression and oscillatory deposition condition
Possible non-optimal torch angle or travel technique, inferred from one-sided lower-toe predominance

reasoning.teacher_uncertainty: no synchronized travel-position signal or arc-voltage trace is available; therefore, the exact spatial location and relative contribution of torch angle versus travel behavior cannot be quantified from the supplied data alone.

downstream_action.inspection: Gauge toe groove depth against ISO 5817 (0.5 mm stringent / 1 mm moderate) before release
downstream_action.process: Verify the programmed current against WPS-014 before the next batch; reduce welding current (kb-v1 remedy edge, w9)
downstream_action.training: Parameter set-up and WPS adherence; torch work-angle consistency (only if H4 is confirmed by added sensing)
downstream_action.memory: Store case with observations, ranked hypotheses, and evidence links

history.note: Aggregation over the dataset's undercut welds, presented as the station's history
